Comments: On April 30, 2026, the Department conducted Routine Complete Inspection of Diversified's Thompson/Bloniarz 1 plugged well located in Georges Township, Fayette County following IR 4167430, where violations were issued for failure to have a site restoration plan on site. Refer to IR 4190461 for the closure of these violations.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on March 7, 2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 3/07/2025, therefore the well site should be fully restored by 12/07/2025 and a well site restoration report should be submitted to the Department by 2/05/2026. Refer to IR 4190445, for the status of the COA.At the time of this inspection, a site restoration plan was observed to be present in an on-site mailbox. The access road to this plugged gas well site was observed to unrestored and graveled. The plugged gas well site was not observed to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. Erosion and sedimentation controls were observed to be removed from the plugged gas well site despite the site not being permanently stabilized. According to the E and S plan on-site CFS is to be installed along the perimeter of the site. Although no active erosion and sedimentation issues were observed at this time, there is the potential for future erosion and sedimentation issues to occur.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued at this time for failure to have E and S controls installed on site until the site is permanently stabilized.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/15/2025 to PA MINERAL SVCS LLC in Unity Township, Westmoreland county. 78.66(a) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to comply with the reporting and corrective action requirements of 25 Pa. Code Section 91.33 when a release of a substance caused or threatened pollution to the Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PA MINERAL SVCS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/15/2025
Violation Code: 78.66(a) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to comply with the reporting and corrective action requirements of 25 Pa. Code Section 91.33 when a release of a substance caused or threatened pollution to the Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8249066
Permit API: 129-24019
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Unity Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/15/2025
Comments: On September 15 2025, the Department conducted an inspection of the E Shuster 2 OG Well in response to an OGI referral of the production tank leaking what appeared to be production fluid.At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled and equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head. During the inspection, it appeared the production tank had previously been leaking and/or overflowed, but did not appear to be actively leaking. The tank appeared to be approximately 80% full at the time of the inspection.At the base of the production tank, there appeared to be an excess amount of fluid along with a thick oil based matter. There appeared to be absorbent mats on the ground next to and under the production tank where the release appeared to have occurred. Based on the amount of fluid on the ground observed by the Department, this appeared to be a reportable release (5 gallons or more). A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.05mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the soil in the area of the spill. While some readings appeared comparable to the background reading, others were elevated in comparison to the background reading. Readings of 0.09mS 0.10mS, 0.14mS 0.31mS, 0.39mS, 0.41mS, 0.49ms, 0.64mS, 1.39mS, 1.33mS were obtained by the Department. Elevated readings were detected in about a 1 foot radius around the production tank.Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted operator representative Joe Miller to inform him of the release. Mr. Miller indicated that they had replaced/repaired a faulty dump valve the week prior. He stated field members would be at the site to assess the area for a release and remediation would occur as necessary. The Department recommended that the Operator take immediate action to remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy.The operator is requested to submit a written response within 7 days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include:1.) An incident report including the quantity and type of fluid released (including the oil based matter) and how this was determined.2.) How long it is believed the release was occurring,3.) A timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.4.) Clarification/waste manifests for any production fluid or other production waste that has been disposed of from the site in the last 2 years.The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid (and/or other fluids) resulting in a release to the ground, as well as failure to report a release.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to BEAR LAKE PROP LLC in Columbus Township, Warren County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/25/2024 to BEAR LAKE PROP LLC in Columbus Township, Warren county. 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BEAR LAKE PROP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/25/2024
Violation Code: 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
Violation ID: 8206014
Permit API: 123-39874
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Columbus Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/25/2024
Comments: The Bittinger 4 disposal injection well is housed inside a shed and is plumbed directly to the Bear Lake Properties, LLC truck unloading area located approximately 1500 feet east of the Bittinger 4 well. Multiple pieces of liner have been placed on the floor of the shed around the well. At this time, standing fluid was visible on the liner. A conductivity meter was used to find that the fluid's conductivity was greater than 20,000 microsiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). The partially exposed dirt floor at the edge of the liner was found to have soils with conductivity greater than 1,000 uS/cm, with some measurements as high as 2,500 uS/cm being observed. The fluid originating from Bittinger 4 traveled southwest from the shed to the edge of the gravel well pad, as evident from the dead vegetation and exposed soils in this direction. The portion of the gravel pad downslope of the shed was noticeably wet despite recent lack of rain. Approximately three feet southwest of the shed, a conductivity reading of 4,000 uS/cm was observed a few inches below the surface of the gravel. Approximately 70 feet southwest of the shed, soil conductivity of 2,330 uS/cm was observed in soils at the edge of the gravel pad.Background soil conductivity measurements were taken across portions of the site in areas that appeared to be unaffected by the release of fluids from Bittinger 4. Background soil conductivity readings between 200 to 300 uS/cm were observed at apparently unimpacted areas near the Bittinger 4 location.After encountering a depression at the edge of the gravel pad, the flow of the fluid was redirected southward. The southward flow was apparent via swaths of dead vegetation and bare soils that appeared to broaden in size and meander about following the terrain. This anastomosing continued for approximately 250 feet between the edge of the gravel pad to where a utility pole was located downslope of Bittinger 4. Near the utility pole, the flow of fluid again channelized and continued approximately 250 feet further down an ATV trail. At this point, as observed by dead vegetation, the majority of the released fluids crossed over the ATV trail and entered a natural drainage swale.Standing water in the drainage swale was found to have an elevated conductivity of 6,100 uS/cm. Soils in the swale were also observed to have elevated conductivity. The impact to this swale continue for approximately 500 feet before the swale transitions into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Brokenstraw Creek.Approximately 700 feet from the point at which the swale transitions into the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek, another stream channel converges with the impacted stream. Conductivity readings in the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek remain downstream from the confluence of the channels with levels observed greater than 1,000 uS/cm. In contrast, water conductivity measured approximately ten feet upstream of the confluence in the unaffected channel was 130 uS/cm.The apparent extent of impact to the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek ends at a point with coordinates reading 41.99407 degrees North by 79.54025 degrees West.On 10/25/24 I called and spoke with John McCollums of Bear Lake Properties, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. John agreed to meet with Department officials early next week to review the release.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Approximately 70 feet southwest of the shed, soil conductivity of 2,330 uS/cm was observed in soils at the edge of the gravel pad.Background soil conductivity measurements were taken across portions of the site in areas that appeared to be unaffected by the release of fluids from Bittinger 4. Background soil conductivity readings between 200 to 300 uS/cm were observed at apparently unimpacted areas near the Bittinger 4 location.After encountering a depression at the edge of the gravel pad, the flow of the fluid was redirected southward. The southward flow was apparent via swaths of dead vegetation and bare soils that appeared to broaden in size and meander about following the terrain. This anastomosing continued for approximately 250 feet between the edge of the gravel pad to where a utility pole was located downslope of Bittinger 4. Near the utility pole, the flow of fluid again channelized and continued approximately 250 feet further down an ATV trail. At this point, as observed by dead vegetation, the majority of the released fluids crossed over the ATV trail and entered a natural drainage swale.Standing water in the drainage swale was found to have an elevated conductivity of 6,100 uS/cm. Soils in the swale were also observed to have elevated conductivity. The impact to this swale continue for approximately 500 feet before the swale transitions into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Brokenstraw Creek.Approximately 700 feet from the point at which the swale transitions into the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek, another stream channel converges with the impacted stream. Conductivity readings in the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek remain downstream from the confluence of the channels with levels observed greater than 1,000 uS/cm. In contrast, water conductivity measured approximately ten feet upstream of the confluence in the unaffected channel was 130 uS/cm.The apparent extent of impact to the UNT of Brokenstraw Creek ends at a point with coordinates reading 41.99407 degrees North by 79.54025 degrees West.On 10/25/24 I called and spoke with John McCollums of Bear Lake Properties, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. John agreed to meet with Department officials early next week to review the release.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Violation ID: 8257659

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 12/03/2025
Comments: On 12/03/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of STL Resources LLC's Thomas 808 multi-well pad located in Elk Township, Tioga County. Upon arrival to the site at 0930 hours, weather was 28F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1). Personnel from STL Resources were present at the time of this inspection.This inspection was conducted in response to a report submitted by STL to the DEP North Central Regional Office on 11/30/2025 at 1300 hours which reported a failure in the Thomas 808 5H gas processing unit (GPU) ethylene glycol water bath system which resulted in at least 5 gallons of glycol visibly overflowing from the unit and onto the pad surface (CID #393888).Discussions with STL personnel revealed that the GPU experienced a failure of a temperature gauge on the ethylene glycol-water bath system (photo #2). As a result, the ethylene glycol-water mixture overheated and leaked onto the pad surface. At the time of this inspection, an estimated 25-30 gallons of ethylene glycol leaked out of the unit (photos #3 and 4). This estimate was calculated by comparing the level of ethylene glycol which remained in the 5H GPU after the leak with the full 2H GPU (photos #5 and 6). STL is working on determining an exact amount at this time.Personnel from STL were onsite and had already begun disassembling and removing the GPU and beginning remediation of the impacted area (photo #7). On Friday, 12/5/2025, a crane and vacuum truck is scheduled to arrive onsite to remove the GPU and the remainder of the impacted pad material. The impacted pad material will be removed from the site and sent to Waste Management for characterization and disposal.Based upon the release of an estimated 25-30 gallons of glycol onto the pad surface from the 5H GPU, a violation of 35 P.S. 691.402(b) is cited against API #117-20478.I departed the site at 1030 hours.

Comments: On 8/10/23 at 1201 hrs., I conducted an incident inspection of Madtick Development Corp.'s Musser Associates 2 well site (API 063-32934) in East Mahoning Twp., Indiana Co. The inspection was conducted in response to a phone call received on 8/10/23 from the landowner, indicating that a production fluid release was observed at the well site. The landowner unsuccessfully attempted to contact the operator, and then reported the release to the Department. Upon inspection of the site, stressed/dead vegetation was observed around the production fluid tank onsite, and in an adjacent corn field. The area of dead vegetation appears to be approximately 30-45 feet wide and extends approximately 200-250 feet to the North of the well site. The release appears to be originating from a tank onsite. The tank appears to be empty. The release appears to be over 1 barrel of fluid. In addition to the release, it was observed that the well is equipped for production. A well tag is not affixed to the completed well. A site ID sign is posted, but is illegible and does not display the required information.Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), and 78.66(b) are being cited for failure by the operator to report the release, and are immediately being closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of OGA 3211(G) and OGA 3211(H) are cited for the lack of site ID sign and well tag. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1) are cited for the release of production fluids from the tank onto the ground. The violations will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release anddemonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 10/10/2023
Comments: On 10/10/2023, I conducted an inspection due to an incident that occurred on 10/06/2023. A gathering line inside of the tank battery containment which is located 290 feet to the south from the Arnold #2, had failed and crude oil traveled down slope from the tank battery area, aprox. 90 feet away. A neighbor had complained to the pumper, reporting that they smelled gas on Wednesday October 5th or Thursday October 6th. The pumper had looked around and found nothing on those days. On the evening of Friday October 6th crude was discovered inside and outside the containment. Sam Harvey of Bull Run notified the Department of the release on the Arnold lease owned by Armac Resources on Saturday October 7th.The gathering line ran through the dike wall, it is not clear whether the dike wall failed or if the line leaked outside of containment or both. Crude oil is visible outside of containment. When I arrived on site, the area as seen in the photos was already mulched and seeded. I removed several patches of mulch and smelled the soil underneath he mulch, the soil had a strong distinct smell of crude oil. The southwest side of the dike wall has been excavated and the contaminated material was placed inside of a roll off that remains onsite. It is unclear how much if any soil has been removed in the downslope area below the tank battery.There is no evidence of production fluid in the road ditch located along Bauer Hill road. A boom has been placed in the dry ditch as a precaution. I spoke with Sam Harvey and Justin Hansen of Bull Run (who are contract pumping and facilitating the clean up for Armac Resources). I suggested that an underflow dam be placed at the bottom of the area that has been mulched (base of hill), this is to prevent any remaining production fluid from being washed down to the road side ditch of Bauer Hill which leads to an unnamed tributary of Glade Run.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT CHAP LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/15/2024
Violation Code: 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8188101
Permit API: 129-28483
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Sewickley Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2024
Comments: On May 15, 2024 the Department conducted a follow up inspection of EQTs Cook Unit 17H well pad in response to IR 3747032 where violations were issued for failure to maintain PCSM BMPs. At the time of the inspection, the Act 9 sign was present at the entrance of the access road which appeared stabilized and the ERP was present in the on-site mailbox. There are two wells on this pad that appeared to be equipped for production and are surrounded by cement barriers. Well 17H has it's well tag present with all necessary information posted, and no fluid discharges or fluid leaks were observed from/near the wellhead. The 17H GPU was surrounded by cement barriers and was not in secondary containment however, well 17H has a SPUD date prior to the October 2016 proclamation of chapter 78a, therefore secondary containment is not required to be installed. The 17H production tank was in secondary containment that had fluid pooled in it and was surrounded by cement barriers. The production tank appeared to be equipped for production with no observable fluid leaks or fluid discharge coming from it. The Department is again recommend the Operator continue to monitor the secondary containment to ensure that fluid currently in it will not inhibit its 110% hold capacity requirements. Upon inspection of the perimeter of the well site, at least 70% vegetative growth was seen throughout, as well as two riprap aprons. The riprap apron at the front of the well site did not show any erosion or sedimentation concerns, however the riprap apron at the rear of the well site (where violations were initially issued for during IR 3747032) still appears to be in violation. It is apparent that some riprap was added to the outlet and that some seeding/mulching was done by the appearance of vegetation looking fuller behind the riprap outlet, but pooling of fluid and saturated grass can be seen directly behind the riprap outlet and follows the channel that was once leading to the agricultural field behind the well site. While on site, the department contacted Jeremy Barber a representative of EQT to let them know that the riprap apron is still failing to prevent channelize flow from occurring. Jeremy stated that they will be sending an NOV response on May 16, 2024 notating that some maintenance was done and that they plan to continue to monitor it. Jeremy also stated that EQT would beef up the riprap apron some more to hopefully prevent this channelize flow from continuing to occur, and is going to think of a way to further prevent this without effecting all the grass surrounding the well site. Jeremy will set up a walk through of the well site with the Department after more maintenance is done on the riprap outlet.Based on todays inspection, violations issued under IR 3747032 will remain outstanding for failure to maintain PCSM BMPs.

I recommend that fluid from inside the battery is not migrate through the berm. Livestock activity in the vicinity is taken into consideration (Photos 13-17). Violation ID: 8242765
Permit API: 117-22232
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Lawrence Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/30/2025
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at JKLM Energy's TSF 12 Well Site located in Lawrence Township, Tioga County on 7/30/2025 at 1110 hours. The weather was 85 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by JKLM. JKLM reported that on 7/30/2025 at ~0801 hours, a pressure regulating "Kimray" valve on a gas production unit's dump line washed out on the bottom. The washout resulted in a spray/mist of produced fluids to reach the pad surface impacting the gravel material. An estimated 25 to 35 gallons of produced fluids was released to the pad surface. An area ~16ft by 13ft by ~2 inches deep was delineated as impacted. JKLM reported that the production unit dumps ~three quarters of a barrel of produced fluids through the line at intervals and only one dump interval was able to escape the line.During my inspection, the valve was in the process of being replaced. A hydrovac truck was dispatched and was en route to the site for remediation to begin. Due to the release being under and around piping infrastructure, the hydrovac will be utilized to recover impacted material rather than using excavation equipment. The impacted area can be seen in photo #2. I field measured the pad material within the impacted area and received readings for electrical conductivity ranging from 2.7 to >4.0mS/cm. Once collected, the impacted material will be stored in a residual waste container for later disposal. A representative with JKLM will be using a soil probe to guide the remediation efforts. The hydrovac truck arrived onsite prior to my departure. JKLM later provided me with an update and photos of the area after remediation was completed (see photos #3 and 4). After removing material, it was noted that excavation efforts went 7-8 inches deep in some spots where the fluids were stopped by a soil cement layer. The area was cleaned up to visible.Based on the findings of this inspection report, the following violations are cited as immediately corrected against API #117-22232:CSL 402(b), 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a), and SWMA 301I departed the site at 1205 hours.

Violation ID: 8198912
Permit API: 051-21047
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Dunbar Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/19/2024
Comments: On August 19, 2024 the Department (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of State Game Lands 51B1 Well located in Dunbar Township, Fayette County, where violations were continued for a release from production equipment inside the green shed.At the time of this inspection, Minor rutting is developing in the access road as it enters the well site; therefore, the Department recommends the operator continue to monitor and maintain the access road as necessary in order to prevent any erosion and sedimentation events from occurring. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniformand adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the area where a production tank had previously been placed. The DEP recommends this area be seeded and mulched. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection.Two production tanks within secondary containment were observed. One of the production tanks appeared rusted but no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed. However, the tank's secondary containment was nearly full of fluid. The DEP recommends that the containment be drained, fluid be disposed of properly, and in accordance with regulations. The well tag was present at the time of this inspection. A well tag was found on the ground near wellhead. The Dept recommends the Operator permanently affix the well tag in accordance with 3211(h) . There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. No fluid discharges were observed coming from the production tank near the wellhead onsite, however, the production tanks lid was cracked in half and open and there appeared to be a high level of fluid in this production tank. The DEP recommends the Operator replace the lid on this production tank and properly dispose of the contents within this tank to prevent a potential release. The production tank near the green shed had a hose inside the secondary containment extending out onto the ground. It appears that water in the secondary containment is being discharged to the ground as the secondary containment is at capacity. The Department recommends the removal of this excess fluid in accordance with current regulations to accommodate any potential releases that may occur. Inside the green shed located on this well site, a compressor station as well as various barrels with various unknown substances not in containment were observed. Some barrels were heavily rusted and staining in the gravel was observed underneath them as well as under the GPU and production equipment. The Department request the Operator provide information on what exactly is in the drums and what they are being used for. The Department request that this information be provided with the NOV response. The Department also recommends that the Operator remove all equipment/supplies not necessary for production.Inside the green shed, the spill that was previously observed in inspection reports 3743832 and 3808945 remains. In this green shed, the spill appears to be an oily like petroleum substance on the ground. The DEP again recommends that the Operator remediate the areas as necessary in accordance with the Department's Spill Policy. The DEP again requests the operator evaluate the releases that have occurred and provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. The GPU unit (not in secondary containment) in this green shed had no observable active leaks or discharge.Based on today's inspection violations for the spill shall remain outstanding along with failure to have the well tag permanently affixed to the wellhead.

Comments: I arrived to the location at 12:50pm. The weather was 68¿¿F and sunny at time of inspection. I met with Repsol representative Billy Watts on location for the inspection. Plugging work was being performed on this well (9H) at time of inspection. A gel plug was set in the hole with a top at 2,630'. The rig was planning to next run a Cement Bond Log (CBL) and continue with plugging operations. On 9/21/2023 (prior to my arrival onsite), the production casing was section milled and approximately 13’ of damaged casing was removed from the well. I visually inspected the section of removed casing during this inspection. The piece of casing that was on top of the 5 1/2" production casing string was a 3' pup joint. Approximately 1 1/2' down the 3' pup joint, 3 holes were noted in the casing. The dimensions of the holes ranged in size from approximately 1/8" to 2" and varied from a straight-lined crack to irregular and rounded in shape. While the damaged casing was visually observed during the inspection, Repsol did restrict my ability to document the condition of the removed section of casing by photograph. Although, Repsol provided photographs of the removed section of casing to the Department the next day (9/22/2023), this represents a violation of Section 3258(a) of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. ¿¿ 3258(a). I left the location at 1:45pm. In addition to citing this new violation, the outstanding violations that were previously cited (Inspection Record #3611541) were also noted as continuing during this inspection. Therefore, the Inspection Results Code used for this inspection report is Violation(s) and Recurring Violations (VRV). The PADEP requests that Respol include an explanation of the cause of this violation with the written response previously-requested in the NOV dated 8/28/2023 (Inspection Record #3611541).

Report Details

Violation ID: 984485

Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/08/2023
Comments: On February 8, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Kiskiminetas Spring School 4 well in Loyalhanna Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3488724, where high conductivity was found underneath the brine tank valve. The Department had yet to receive the waste manifest from remediation or the quantity released in the spill noted in IR 3307023, therefore the Department was unable to assess whether the spill had been remediated in accordance with DEP Spill Policy. Violations were continued as a result, and the Department requested that the operator provide the waste manifest and any other relevant information no later than February 10, 2023. Heavy tire rutting was also observed on the access road. Present were myself, DEP OGI Curtis Small, Brian Haney from PA Mineral Services, and Joe Miller from Mid Atlantic Energy Services. The following was observed:The well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns related to E and S or vegetative coverage (see photo 7). The API number and operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 4). This information now reflects the information that the Department has on file. A hissing sound and a strong gas odor was observed coming from the well head at the time of inspection (see photo 5). Mr. Haney and Mr. Miller were making repairs on the well head at the time of inspection. The brine tank appeared to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 3). However, elevated conductivity remains underneath the brine tank valve (see photo 1). A background soil conductivity reading was taken along the access road, which read 120 Microsiemens (see photo 9). Heavy tire rutting remains in the access road (see photo 8). It was initially noted that the access road is shared with the operator and Kiski Prep School. However, Mr. Haney informed the Department that unrelated timber trucks also use the access road for removal of trees for timber. Trees that are said to be marked for timber use could be observed north of the well site (see photo 6).Based on observations from this inspection, the the Department recommends that the operator investigate the cause of the elevated conductivity and remediate accordingly. Violations remain outstanding. The Department also recommends that the operator cooperatively monitor and maintain the access road with Kiski School, and Timber companies that use it to prevent accelerated erosion. The Department requests that the operator provide the waste manifest and any other relevant information, including quantity released no later than February 10, 2023.

Permit API: 081-21894
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/29/2022
Comments: On November 29, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the Beech Resources ISA Well Pad. At the time of inspection, Beech Resources was in stimulation operations of the recently drilled wells. An area of elevated soil conductivity was observed off the west end of the well pad in an area that was recently backfilled due to a developed erosion channel. The DEP screened the surrounding area and found the area of elevated conductivity to be approximately 180 ft. x 30 ft. This area encompasses the top of the well pad slope down past the compost filter socks in place and about 20 ft. past the compost filter sock. Soil conductivity in the area of impact ranged from 1,500 uS/cm to over range reading of the soil conductivity meter. The upper limit of the soil conductivity meter is 4,000 uS/cm. Soil sample 0651-141 was collected from the area of impact. During the inspection, Don Stevenson with Beech Resources arrived onsite. DEP showed Mr. Stevenson where the area of elevated conductivity was found off the west end of the pad slope. While DEP was still onsite, Mr. Stevenson called to have an excavator sent to the well pad. Mr. Stevenson said Penn E and R was also called to schedule a time to delineate the spill. Due to the unknown volume of the spill, Beech Resources plans to clean up the area under the Act 2 remediation requirments. During the inspection, another area was observed off the southwest corner of the well pad where an erosion channel had formed at the top of the well pad slope and continued down past the compost filter sock off the permitted limit of disturbance. This area was also shown to Mr. Stevenson and he said that Beech Resources will dress up compost filter socks and backfill the channel that has formed.Much of the site has become vegetated. Temporary E and S controls are still in place and are in good condition except for the previously mentioned areas.The area of elevated levels of conductivity outside of containment off the well pad edge is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b). Additional violations could be assessed pending results from the soil sample collected. An erosion channel has formed at the top of the well pad slope and continues off the permitted limit of disturbance conveying sediment off the permitted site is an additional violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b) and Chapter 102.11(a)1.

Comments: On 03/21/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Hixenbaugh 1-P060 Well Site following violations issued on 02/14/2024 (Inspection Report 3713663, Enforcement ID 425992). Violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, and 91.34(a) were issued to the operator for the Department's discovery of oil/grease on the ground at various locations around the well site. The following was observed during inspection on 03/21/2024:The larger area of oil/grease on the ground next to the compressor was removed and new gravel was added. Gravel moved aside to view soils beneath - the oil/grease was removed, clean soils noted (Photos 1-3). The section of oil/grease along the side of the compressor fence/tarp had been removed, some residuals noted along fence line. New gravel added (Photo 4).A waste barrel was noted on site; it was unclear if there was waste within, however I recomend that any waste be removed from site and a manifest be submitted to the Department as soon as possible. Containment was noted (yellow container) next to compressor; buckets on containment (Photos 1, 2). Per the operator's response, they plan to remove the waste barrel pending contractor availability and weather conditions (dated 03/07/2024).It looked as though oil/grease was cleaned up next to the compressor and the trough. I recommend that any oil/grease on the ground be cleaned up as soon as possible and the levels within the trough are monitored (Photos 5-7).A small section of oil/grease was noted on the ground next to the piping that previously displayed tubing. It looked as though repairs were made and the tubing was removed. I recommend that any remaining oil/grease be removed from the ground (Photos 8, 9).The disturbance next to the earthen berm was addressed. A liner and gravel were added along this path. I recommend precautions are taken so that water does not travel underneath the liner and cause accelerated erosion (Photos 10-12). A wet spot was noted on the gravel, however this spot did not display elevated conductivity readings. A small area below the berm drain appeared wet; this area also did not display elevated conductivity readings (Photos 12, 13).The production tank was replaced and gravel was added within the berm and under the new tank. There was a wet spot noted below the piping on the tank, however no elevated conductivity readings were noted (Photos 14, 15).The oil/grease on the ground around the wellhead was removed. Clean soils were noted below the added gravel. I recommend that the wellhead is monitored to avoid any additional oil/grease from reaching the ground (Photos 16, 17). Additional gravel added around production equipment (Photo 18).A buffalo was noted onsite, however contents unknown. Although not required, I recommend that this is placed on containment to avoid any materials from reaching the ground (Photos 18, 19).The access road was in relatively good condition. Some tire ruts noted. There was a pile of dirt next to the road. I recommend that this is removed to avoid any sediment laden runoff, as there is a culvert outlet leading down slope and is approximately 35 feet downslope of this pile (Photo 22).Minor erosion noted at the beginning of the access road leading off into the vegetation. There is a spring on the bank below this area. I recommend that this area of erosion is addressed to avoid any sediment laden water from reaching the main road (Photos 23-25). The violations issued on 02/14/2024 remain outstanding. No additional violations are being issued at this time.

Violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, and 91.34(a) were issued to the operator for the Department's discovery of oil/grease on the ground at various locations around the well site. The following was observed during inspection on 03/21/2024:The larger area of oil/grease on the ground next to the compressor was removed and new gravel was added. Gravel moved aside to view soils beneath - the oil/grease was removed, clean soils noted (Photos 1-3). The section of oil/grease along the side of the compressor fence/tarp had been removed, some residuals noted along fence line. New gravel added (Photo 4).A waste barrel was noted on site; it was unclear if there was waste within, however I recomend that any waste be removed from site and a manifest be submitted to the Department as soon as possible. Containment was noted (yellow container) next to compressor; buckets on containment (Photos 1, 2). Per the operator's response, they plan to remove the waste barrel pending contractor availability and weather conditions (dated 03/07/2024).It looked as though oil/grease was cleaned up next to the compressor and the trough. I recommend that any oil/grease on the ground be cleaned up as soon as possible and the levels within the trough are monitored (Photos 5-7).A small section of oil/grease was noted on the ground next to the piping that previously displayed tubing. It looked as though repairs were made and the tubing was removed. I recommend that any remaining oil/grease be removed from the ground (Photos 8, 9).The disturbance next to the earthen berm was addressed. A liner and gravel were added along this path. I recommend precautions are taken so that water does not travel underneath the liner and cause accelerated erosion (Photos 10-12). A wet spot was noted on the gravel, however this spot did not display elevated conductivity readings. A small area below the berm drain appeared wet; this area also did not display elevated conductivity readings (Photos 12, 13).The production tank was replaced and gravel was added within the berm and under the new tank. There was a wet spot noted below the piping on the tank, however no elevated conductivity readings were noted (Photos 14, 15).The oil/grease on the ground around the wellhead was removed. Clean soils were noted below the added gravel. I recommend that the wellhead is monitored to avoid any additional oil/grease from reaching the ground (Photos 16, 17). Additional gravel added around production equipment (Photo 18).A buffalo was noted onsite, however contents unknown. Although not required, I recommend that this is placed on containment to avoid any materials from reaching the ground (Photos 18, 19).The access road was in relatively good condition. Some tire ruts noted. There was a pile of dirt next to the road. I recommend that this is removed to avoid any sediment laden runoff, as there is a culvert outlet leading down slope and is approximately 35 feet downslope of this pile (Photo 22).Minor erosion noted at the beginning of the access road leading off into the vegetation. There is a spring on the bank below this area. I recommend that this area of erosion is addressed to avoid any sediment laden water from reaching the main road (Photos 23-25). The violations issued on 02/14/2024 remain outstanding. No additional violations are being issued at this time.
